newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan government, strikers agree to meet.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan government, strikers agree to meet.

text.p: Nicaragua's squabbling factions took a step closer to resolving a four-day-old national strike Thursday when President Arnoldo Aleman agreed to meet with the leaders of the Sandinista-led strike.

After a three-hour meeting with former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega, the two men agreed to meet again Friday with representatives of the striking sectors, who are protesting the right-wing government's economic policies that they say are pushing people out of work.

"We agreed on many aspects of the national reality and we are going to finish (the talks) tomorrow when we meet with Commander Ortega and the sectors involved in the strike in the presidential palace," Aleman told reporters.

He also said he would send to Nicaragua's National Assembly a bill that would suspend for three months the court-ordered evictions of farmers who received confiscated land during the Sandinista land reform in the 1980s.
A key demand of the strikers is that they receive legal titles to the confiscated property they received and that a wave of evictions by the former owners be halted.
